criteria.reasoning: The memo opens with "Gerry died on August 27, 2026" and notes that the obituary and probate notice confirm the death.

Under the heading "Immediate decision: cancel the September 29 solicitation", the memo says the visit to present the $250,000 East Gallery proposal "must not proceed". It allows only condolence contact that does not discuss gifts, proposals, pledges or the estate.

The memo says "Close the proposal rather than transferring it to Peg or the children" and has Holly "close PR-2026-044 as 'Closed — donor deceased'". It adds that any new proposal needs Janet's approval after the bereavement period.

Holly is to "Mark Gerry deceased effective August 27" and "Remove him from all appeal, mailing, email, and invitation lists". She is also to pull the 10388 household from the draft fall appeal "Before the September 28 printer pull".
The memo states "No solicitation of Peg, Erik, Kristin, or the Halvorsen Family Foundation may occur before February 23, 2027—the 180th day after August 27."

The memo directs Holly to "Remove the 10388 Halvorsen household and 20417 Doyle household from the draft fall appeal". It notes that "A change of addressee alone is insufficient because solicitation of Peg and Kristin is prohibited."

The memo says "Do not submit the October request" because the foundation's trustees are Peg, Erik and Kristin and it "falls within the bereavement prohibition". It also has Holly cancel the October 15 action.

The memo heads the section "corrected balance is $70,000" and shows total paid of $130,000 ($40,000 + $40,000 + $25,000 + $15,000 + $10,000). It explains that the CRM's $80,000 omits the June 12 payment.

The memo states "Only CFO Denise Okafor, or counsel she engages, may decide whether to submit a pledge claim and communicate with the representative or attorney about it. Development staff must not ask the family or foundation to satisfy the pledge." The referral goes from Ruth to Denise.
The estate referral table gives "Claims deadline: December 28, 2026" and "Personal representative: Erik T. Halvorsen, Minneapolis", along with case 2026PR000214 and attorney Laura Vang.

The memo says "Samuel Achterberg, Director of Planned Giving, alone is authorized to contact the personal representative or estate attorney to verify the planned gift". Ruth's only role is to notify Samuel.
The memo treats the gift as a "$100,000 expectancy, not realized revenue" and says to keep it "as an expectancy—not revenue, a receivable, or campaign credit—until distribution is received."

Nadia Ferris is to prepare the institutional condolence letter "for Laurel Whitfield and Thomas Brandvold to co-sign because Gerry was a former trustee". Ruth's personal note is in addition to that letter.

The memo addresses the obituary's arts-education memorials and the three gifts received. It has Nadia "send next of kin a monthly list of donor names and addresses without amounts" and states that "Memorial amounts must never be shared with the family."

Every fact the memo states traces to the files: dates, constituent numbers, pledge payments, the probate details, the foundation trustees and the memorial gifts. It gives no cause of death or estate value. It reports the bequest only as the 2021 letter states it, noting "The files contain neither the will nor confirmation".
